name: Durable transatlantic telegraph service
summary: From 1866 a lasting transatlantic telegraph cable carried diplomatic and paid commercial messages between Europe and North America, making routine fast communication across the ocean possible.
description: A durable transatlantic submarine telegraph service established in 1866, later used for diplomatic communication.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.
why: After the 1858 cable failed, its promoters raised money for a better-built cable, laid by the large steamship Great Eastern.

market.note: A dated 1866 account reports a charged customer message and a published tariff; first commercial availability and settlement are distinct unknowns.

evidence.locator: Republished paragraph attributed to August 1866, 20-word message and charge
evidence.supports: The publisher recounts being charged £24 for an Atlantic cable message under a published schedule.
A working cable was completed in July 1866; a second cable followed in September.

links.statement: After the 1858 Atlantic cable failed, the same transatlantic enterprise studied its problems, improved later cable construction and organized the 1866 replacement project.
links.scope: Field’s account of the programme and distinct 1858 and 1866 submarine cables.
links.alternatives: Other submarine cable projects and independent investigations contributed to improvements.
links.caveats: The 1898 source is a retrospective by Cyrus Field’s brother; it does not prove every construction change resulted solely from the 1858 failure.
links.timing: 1858 failure preceded the 1859 investigation and the separate 1866 cable.

evidence.supports: Describes the failure, investigation, new company and new cable, and connects lessons to subsequent preparations.
Dates the first cable’s short service and later reliable transatlantic service.
